claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd can exist as a fully homogenized, chemically disordered FCC alloy after solution treatment.
As-solutionized equiatomic FeCoNiPd exhibits soft ferromagnetism.
Intermediate-temperature annealing can induce nanoscale chemical ordering in equiatomic FeCoNiPd.
Annealing at approximately 700 °C for 2 hours followed by cooling at 1–2 °C/min will produce the proposed nanoscale ordering.
The prescribed annealing window can avoid long-range ordering and secondary-phase formation.
Annealing will form coherent, nanoscale chemically ordered clusters within a predominantly disordered FCC matrix.
The nanoscale ordered clusters will locally enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The nanoscale ordered clusters will act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Domain-wall pinning by the ordered clusters will impede domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion will increase the coercive field.
The annealed alloy may exhibit more than a 50% increase in coercivity relative to as-solutionized equiatomic FeCoNiPd.
The annealed alloy will retain high saturation magnetization despite its increased coercivity.
Retention of a predominantly disordered matrix will preserve high saturation magnetization.
The nanoscale-ordering treatment will retain sufficiently high configurational entropy for the material to remain a high-entropy alloy.
Excessive annealing time or an improper cooling rate may cause long-range order or secondary-phase formation.
Long-range ordering or secondary-phase formation would compromise the alloy's high-entropy state.
